transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sara (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Lena (Apex Head of MLOps), James (Platform Eng), Priya (Security)

Summary: quick recap of last week's load tests, discussed autoscaling policy gaps, burst node vs pre-warm pools, KV cache warm-up, and SOC2/KMS questions. Next steps: sizing spreadsheet update, traffic traces, benchmark window.

00:00:05 - Sara: ok hey everyone, thanks for making time, quick roll call, we're on for 45 minutes today, main goal is to go through the pilot results and adjust dedicated sizing and autoscaling for the traffic patterns you saw last week.
00:00:18 - Lena: yeah thanks sara, we really want to nail the cost vs latency tradeoff before the holiday promo tests, plus wanna make sure the burst behaviour is predictable.
00:00:26 - Miguel: cool; i've pulled the logs and the telemetry, i'll share screen in a sec but highlights first — p95 latency spikes when the burst exceeds about 3x baseline qps, and we see a cold-kv penalty for repeat short-conversations.
00:00:40 - James: can you clarify cold-kv penalty? that's the cache of the KV for the generation context right?
00:00:44 - Miguel: yeah so when new sessions come in the kv cache for that session isn't populated and we get extra time on the first few tokens, it's subtle but matters for low-latency routing.
00:00:53 - Priya: from security side quick reminder, we need KMS integration for customer-managed keys and audit logs for all inference requests for compliance; also SOC2 section on data retention, i'll share exact ask later.
00:01:05 - Sara: noted priya, we'll attach the SOC2 and KMS summary in the follow-up, we had flagged audit log retention earlier — Redwood keeps per-request traces for N days by default but we can extend for dedicated tenants.

00:05:12 - Miguel: walking through the sizing spreadsheet — baseline qps we saw was ~120 requests/s with median seq length 80 tokens and heavy tail to 600 tokens. Token/second throughput on the nodes is around 30k tps for the A100 pool when batched, but single-request latency depends on batching window.
00:05:35 - Lena: that baseline sounds right, on peak promo we saw bursts to ~380 rps for short windows (30-90s). The issue last week was that autoscale added nodes too slowly and we hit queueing.
00:05:50 - Miguel: yeah our current autoscale threshold was conservative — scale up at 75% avg utilization with cooldown 120s and max 3 nodes added per minute. For bursts that short, cold start + provisioning time caused queuing.
00:06:10 - James: what's the typical provisioning time for a new dedicated GPU instance in the Redwood Dedicated flow?
00:06:14 - Miguel: we usually see 45-90 seconds to spin up a new GPU pod in Dedicated depending on region and instance type; if you need 0s provisioning we recommend warm-pools or pre-warmed burst nodes instead.
00:06:26 - Lena: so warm-pool is effectively a pool of pre-initialized containers waiting to take traffic? what's the memory/kv state behaviour?
00:06:34 - Miguel: warm-pool keeps the runtime hot — model weights loaded, runtime initialized but not necessarily KV cache populated. We can do a pre-warm step to populate common KV prefixes if you give us typical prompt prefixes. That reduces the cold-kv penalty.
00:06:49 - Priya: any security tradeoffs for warm pools? persistent memory with secrets?
00:06:53 - Miguel: good question — warm-pools still operate under tenant isolation; KMS keys are not held in plaintext in memory, and access controls same as live nodes. We can provide an architecture doc for how keys are handled in warm-pools.

00:10:02 - Sara: ok so proposed changes: lower the autoscale threshold to 60% for scale-up during the pilot, reduce cooldown to 30s for aggressive ramp, and enable a small warm-pool sized for expected burst amplitude — say for 3x baseline add 4 warm nodes. We'll model cost impact in the spreadsheet.
00:10:21 - James: 4 warm nodes — is that per-AZ or per-cluster? we run multi-AZ.
00:10:25 - Miguel: that's a great point — sizing per-AZ is recommended. the spreadsheet assumes even distribution; if your traffic is single-region heavy we'll adjust.
00:10:35 - Lena: during last test one AZ got hammered more than others because of our DNS routing, so ideally we size warm-pool per-AZ and have staggered warmup.
00:10:45 - Sara: we'll add an AZ-aware column to the sizing sheet, good catch.

00:13:40 - Miguel: another optimization — adaptive batching for short requests: we can set a max batch latency window (e.g., 10ms) so we don't wait too long to fill a batch, that keeps single-request latencies down while getting throughput benefits. There is a tradeoff in cpu overhead.
00:13:58 - James: will that impact cost significantly?
00:14:01 - Miguel: minimal; batching increases throughput and reduces per-token cost, but for ultra low-latency you tune the window smaller and accept some throughput loss. We'll show estimated token-cost vs p95 latency in the model.

00:16:12 - Lena: what about model variants — are there cheaper quantized options for the inference path to lower burst cost?
00:16:18 - Miguel: yes we can run a quantized variant (4-bit) for lower cost; Redwood supports transparent routing so you can have a cheaper fallback during bursts. But there's a small quality delta; recommend A/B test on a holdout set.
00:16:33 - Lena: ok we can do quality evals, we'll include sample prompts.

00:18:50 - Priya: security checklist — SSO/SAML for console, RBAC for team members, KMS CMK support, SOC2 report, and log retention tie-up. Can you confirm default retention and options?
00:19:00 - Sara: default audit retention is 30 days for hosted but for Dedicated we can configurable to 365 or longer as an add-on. We'll include explicit options in the follow-up note.
00:19:11 - Priya: perfect, and one more — need assurance that warm-pool nodes don't hold long-term plaintext keys in memory.
00:19:18 - Miguel: confirmed, keys are fetched on-demand and never persisted to disk; we'll send a short note on the runtime key lifecycle.

00:22:02 - Miguel: back to benchmarking — we propose a 2-hour window where you replay recorded traces (sanitized) with a mix of short and long sequences, and we run three autoscale configs: conservative (current), aggressive scale-up with warm-pool, and aggressive plus quantized fallback. That should show cost/latency differences.
00:22:20 - James: we can do the replay but need guidance on trace format, we'll export nginx logs and app-layer request bodies.
00:22:28 - Sara: we'll send the replay template; James if you can provide the 7-day traces (anonymized) by the 20th we'll schedule the benchmark on the 24th as discussed.

00:25:40 - Lena: in terms of alerts and SLAs, can Redwood alert us when warm-pool is exhausted or when scale-up is triggered? We want hooks into our incident channels.
00:25:52 - Miguel: yes, we can emit events to your webhook or integrate with PagerDuty. We'll provide per-route metrics and alerts; also a per-tenant dashboard in Console for warm-pool usage, scaling events, and cost burn.

00:28:10 - James: curious about cost model for warm-pools billed — is it reserved capacity or billed as on-demand while warm?
00:28:16 - Sara: warm-pool is billed as reserved dedicated nodes while allocated; for short pilots we can offer a burst discount and a blended rate for the first 30 days. We'll include that in the pricing worksheet.

00:30:40 - Miguel: small gotcha on KV warm-up — if you want pre-populated user-level contexts that's possible but needs a pre-warm job that runs your recent sessions; there is a time and cost to populate. For many customers we pre-warm common prompt prefixes which gets most benefit.
00:30:59 - Lena: we'll provide sample prefixes and top-100 templates, that should be fine.

00:33:10 - Sara: quick recap — action items: Redwood updates autoscaling doc and sizing spreadsheet (include AZ column and warm-pool costs), Apex provides 7-day traces and prompt prefixes, security to confirm KMS/SOC2 items. Benchmark scheduled for 2026-03-24 pending traces.
00:33:30 - Priya: noted, i'll consolidate security items and send by 3/22.
00:33:37 - James: i'll get the traces exported by 3/20.
00:33:41 - Lena: appreciate it, and please include the cost delta for quantized fallback as well.
00:33:47 - Miguel: will do — we'll include an A/B cost-quality sheet.

00:36:00 - Sara: any final questions?
00:36:03 - James: one minor — did you mention regional warm pools affect failover? If an AZ goes down how does traffic shift?
00:36:10 - Miguel: yes we recommend cross-AZ redundancy on the warm-pool level; traffic will failover to other AZs but with potential added latency as KV caches are cold in failover AZ. We'll document best practices for DNS/route balancing.
00:36:25 - Lena: ok that's fine for our tolerance.
00:36:30 - Priya: also please add an item on maximum data residency options, we may need EU-only for part of the stack later.
00:36:38 - Sara: got it, we'll include residency options in follow-up.

00:39:50 - Sara: thanks everyone — we'll circulate notes, updated spreadsheet, and SOC2/KMS summary. Next sync in two weeks unless we want a quick check after the benchmark.
00:40:02 - Lena: let's do a quick post-benchmark sync, put tentative slot 2026-03-25 16:00 UTC.
00:40:08 - Sara: noted, i'll send calendar invite.
00:40:15 - Meeting end.
